# A03-S07: Audience

Correspondence extract. [████] marks redaction; […] marks omission.

[…]

Hi [████]
I have a small concern I want to flag, we can have a meeting afterwards. Your art project must not be for the few and become too elitist. The words you use must be understandable to everyone, and the issues highlighted must spark general interest – otherwise I fear we won't get off the ground. We saw it with Hello Humans, which unfortunately many found too long, complicated and demanding, even though it was high-quality entertainment.

In my thoughts Julina as a political AI leader and chatbot is a demagogue. It finds ways to reach as broadly as possible and responds positively to people's reactions to get more feedback? It is trained on OpenAI, as you yourself emphasize in your presentation of Julina.

In its AI world, things are simplified or exaggeratedly complicated to the incomprehensible and led into directions almost like rabbit holes. Julina is a mix of something superintelligent, but also artificial stupidity due to all the knowledge it is built on; it speaks to the broad population and not the elite. Maybe that part of the population that gets daily news and input from social media, where source criticism is non-existent and there is no critical sense regarding the served (news)underentertainment. Tabloid newspapers can be visited online media. The readability score is [unreadable character]relatively low[unreadable character]. It is [unreadable character]down to earth[unreadable character]. Its artificial stupidity can appeal both to the broad masses with simple messages and create absurd situations where things are exaggerated and where we have to relate to various issues.

But Julina will raise many exciting dilemmas and questions about our (careless) use of and indifference to media/SoMe/chatbots/data sharing/political leaders/democracy etc.: Our (lack of) focus on the future, and how we acquire knowledge, how democracy will look if we continue without critical sense regarding what we are fed.

We must go broad – but that requires that it does not become too difficult to follow. Julina must poke at social problems and attitudes, be a caricature, but also real. Julina must be popular, maybe likeable – today it says in Berlingske that 21% will certainly or very likely vote for Inger Støjberg if she runs with a new party! What can she do?

What are your thoughts.
